title: Everyone saves $20 more. Then what?
hook: Every household spends $20 less so it can save. Does the whole country save more?

knows: saving = income − spending, and one household that spends less saves more
one person's spending is another's income (count-the-bread-once)
doesNotKnow: that in a simple model with fixed investment, when every household tries to save more, incomes fall until total saving is back where it was

misconception: If every household saves $20 more, the country saves more.
objective: The learner can explain that in a toy economy with fixed investment of $100, a $20 cut in every household's spending raises saving to $120 for one round, then incomes fall from $1,000 to $900 until saving is back at $100, because spending is someone else's income.

claims.text: Under the stated timing, saving jumps to $120 in round 1, then falls back to $100 as income settles at $900.
claims.source: Deterministic recurrence (Demo.tsx series()): spending_t = 80 + 0.8 × income_{t−1}, income_t = spending_t + 100, saving_t = income_{t−1} − spending_t, from income 1,000. Round 1: 880, 980, 120; round 2: 864, 964, 116; round 24: income 900.47 (reads $900), saving 100.12 (reads $100); round 40: 900.01, 100.00 (builder node run, 2026-10-14). The reveal quotes the record set at milestones round1 and settled, which the record row also shows. Brief: company/domains/briefs/economics.md #58.

claims.text: Each $20 not spent was someone else's lost income, so incomes fell until people could save only what businesses invest: $100.
claims.source: Income = spending + investment; at the resting point Y = (80 + 100)/(1 − 0.8) = 900 and saving S = Y − 80 − 0.8Y = 100 = investment. Before the cut, Y = (100 + 100)/0.2 = 1,000 and S = 100 too.

claims.text: Everyone tried to save more; together they earned $100 less and saved the same.
claims.source: Income 1,000 → 900 (difference 100); saving 100 before and after (from c2). The reveal computes 1,000 − recorded income.

claims.text: This is the paradox of thrift.
claims.source: Name of the result in introductory macroeconomics; popularised by J. M. Keynes, The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money (1936). Builder statement from memory, not checked: the fact-checker should confirm the name (and, if wanted, the attribution) or drop it to 'a paradox'. The learner text names no person.

claims.text: If extra saving funded extra investment, the answer would change.
claims.source: Within the model, saving equals investment at the resting point (c2), so total saving moves with investment; it stayed at $100 only because investment is fixed.

claims.text: The lesson is a toy model: spending = a fixed amount + 80% of last round's income, investment fixed at $100, fixed prices, no government or trade.
claims.source: Stage chip 'Model: spending = $80 + 80% of last round's income; investment fixed at $100; fixed prices' and the reveal's 'in a toy model'. Lesson rule. Optional $40 cut chip: settles at income $800, saving $100 (series(40), builder node run).

recall.question: In a simple economy where business investment is fixed, every household decides to spend $50 less so it can save more. Once incomes settle, what has happened to total saving?
options: It rose by the households' extra saving
It is unchanged, because incomes fell
recall.why: One household's spending is another's income. Incomes fall until total saving again equals the fixed investment, so the attempt to save more leaves total saving the same and incomes lower.
